item.mechanism: Breakaway oxidation caused by continuous cracking and spallation of the oxide scale due to the nucleation of voluminous Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7 oxides at the oxide-metal interface, which induces stresses leading to scale failure.
item.supporting_observation: Multiple cracks nucleating on the scale-metal interface and propagating towards the surface; appearance of Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7 oxides after initial TiO2 and VO2 formation.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold at 800 °C where linear kinetics dominate; at 600 °C, V-rich oxides have only indirect influence on cracking rather than being the main reason.
item.alternatives_considered: Evaporation of V2O5 (observed at 700 °C but insufficient at 600 °C to explain cracking); whisker-like morphology of V-rich oxides accelerating oxygen ingress.
quotes: The breakaway oxidation occurs if many cracks form continuously and propagate quickly through the oxide scale.

records.text: Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Breakaway oxidation caused by continuous cracking and spallation of the oxide scale due to the nucleation of voluminous Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7 oxides at the oxide-metal interface, which induces stresses leading to scale failure.. System: AlNbTiVZr 0.25 high-entropy alloy. Conditions: 600 °C, static lab air, 20–100 h exposure. Evidence: inferred. Observation: Multiple cracks nucleating on the scale-metal interface and propagating towards the surface; appearance of Nb2O5 and TiNb2O7 oxides after initial TiO2 and VO2 formation.. Scope limits: Does not hold at 800 °C where linear kinetics dominate; at 600 °C, V-rich oxides have only indirect influence on cracking rather than being the main reason.. Alternatives: Evaporation of V2O5 (observed at 700 °C but insufficient at 600 °C to explain cracking); whisker-like morphology of V-rich oxides accelerating oxygen ingress.. Quote: "The breakaway oxidation occurs if many cracks form continuously and propagate quickly through the oxide scale."

item.mechanism: Acceleration of oxidation rate due to partial evaporation of volatile V2O5 oxide, which activates breakaway oxidation and deteriorates scale adherence.
item.supporting_observation: Decrease in quantity and intensity of V2O5 oxide diffraction peaks after testing; transition from nearly parabolic to mixed parabolic-linear kinetics.
item.scope_limits: Not the primary mechanism at 600 °C where V2O5 remains stable; effect is specific to temperatures where V2O5 evaporation becomes significant.
item.alternatives_considered: Formation of complex oxides (Nb2O5, TiNb2O7) causing stress; whisker morphology of V-oxides.
quotes: Most probably, the acceleration of oxidation at the second stage was caused by an effect similar to breakaway oxidation.

item.mechanism: Severe linear oxidation driven by pores formed from the evaporation of volatile V-rich oxides (particularly V2O5), which serve as channels for accelerated oxygen ingress to the bare metal.
item.supporting_observation: Linear oxidation kinetics (n=0.92); presence of multiple pores in the oxide scale and at former sites of Zr-rich particles; formation of complex unprotective oxides.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism assumes evaporation of V-oxides is the primary driver; at 900 °C, this process occurs more rapidly leading to disintegration.
item.alternatives_considered: Formation of protective AlNbO4 (negated by V presence); formation of TiNb2O7 and Nb2Zr6O17 which are unprotective.
quotes: The main reason for severe oxidation were the pores, which served as places for accelerated ingress of oxygen toward the bare metal, and appeared as a result of the evaporation of V-rich oxides.

In addition, the evaporation causes the appearance of multiple pores that serve as places for accelerated ingress of oxygen toward the bare metal and thus stands as the main reason for severe oxidation at 800 °C.

item.mechanism: V-hindering of protective oxide formation and facilitation of unprotective complex oxide nucleation (TiNb2O7, Nb2Zr6O17), leading to poor oxidation resistance even in the presence of Al.
item.supporting_observation: Comparison with V-free AlNbTiZr alloy showing 5–12 times lower mass gain; presence of complex oxides instead of protective AlNbO4 or TiO2 layers.
item.scope_limits: Hypothesis applies to V-containing alloys; does not hold for V-free alloys where AlNbO4 formation improves resistance.
item.alternatives_considered: Addition of Al to NbTiZrV (does not enhance resistance); hypothetical doping of AlNbTiZr with V (accelerates oxidation).
quotes: V hinders the formation of protective oxides and facilitates the nucleation of unprotective ones.
This finding confirms that V is largely responsible for the poor oxidation resistance of the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy.

item.mechanism: Heterogeneous oxidation development at lower temperatures where different grains oxidize at different rates, leading to the formation of fine oxide nodules and whiskers.
item.supporting_observation: Discrepancy in topographic appearance of different grains; presence of very fine oxide nodules; surface layer depleted of Zr.
item.scope_limits: Not observed at 800 °C where oxidation is homogeneous; specific to the initial stage of oxidation at 600 °C.
quotes: At 600 °C (Figure 5 a), the oxidation developed heterogeneously, which is evident from the discrepancy in the topographic appearance of different grains.
In addition, very fine oxide nodules were found (magnified insert in Figure 5 a).
At 600 °C (0.5 h) the surface layer contained, besides oxygen, almost equal amounts of Al, Nb, Ti, and V, and was depleted of Zr.

item.mechanism: Oxidation front ascends easily along Zr5Al3 particles while being slightly impeded by the B2 phase, leading to localized dissolution of Zr-rich particles and formation of Nb2Zr6O17 oxides.
item.supporting_observation: EDS maps showing depletion of Al and segregation of V near Zr5Al3 particles; formation of Nb2Zr6O17 particles on borders of former Zr-rich particles; pores at former particle sites.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the transition zone between oxide scale and substrate; relies on the presence of Zr5Al3 particles in the initial microstructure.
quotes: In addition, a lot of pores were found at the former sites of the Zr-rich particles.

item.mechanism: Sample disintegration due to rapid oxidation mechanisms similar to those at 800 °C but occurring more rapidly, driven by V-oxide evaporation and pore formation.
item.supporting_observation: Specimen disintegrated after 50 h; high specific mass gain (225.5 mg/cm2); surface layer comprised of complex oxides (TiNb2O7, AlNbO4, Nb2Zr6O17).
item.scope_limits: Mechanism assumed based on extrapolation from 800 °C behavior; not directly observed due to sample failure.
item.alternatives_considered: Pesting phenomenon (observed in other alloys but not explicitly stated for this alloy at 900 °C).
quotes: At 900 °C, the specimen disintegrated after 50 h of testing.
It can be assumed that the same processes, but in a more rapid manner, are responsible for the disintegration of the sample tested at 900 °C.
The same oxidation mechanisms were assumed to act at 900 °C that led to the disintegration of the specimen after 50 h.
